extracted.intended_audience: inventors and small business owners seeking free patent legal assistance; volunteer patent attorneys and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Information and eligibility requirements for the USPTO Patent Pro Bono Program, including who may receive free patent-preparation help and who may volunteer. Covers common admission guidelines, how to apply, volunteer sign-up, and related pro bono programs (PTAB/TTAB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Income requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: gross household income less than three times the federal poverty level guidelines (though some regional programs may have different criteria)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a common eligibility threshold across the national network, but specific income criteria may vary by regional program. Contact your regional program via the Patent Pro Bono Coverage Map for exact income limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: demonstrated understanding of the patent system either by having a provisional application already on file with the USPTO or having successfully completed the certificate training course (certificado de formación en español)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of basic patent-system knowledge is required so volunteers can work effectively with applicants; regional programs may accept different proofs of knowledge—check the regional program's application page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: ability to describe the particular features of your invention and how it works
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be able to explain the invention's key features and operation so a volunteer practitioner can prepare a patent application; level/detail expectations can vary by region—see local program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific eligibility variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Because specific income, knowledge, and invention requirements vary by program, applicants must consult their regional program for specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Patent Pro Bono Coverage Map to select your state and view the regional program's online application form and precise admission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application method / coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: All regional programs provide online application forms for free patent assistance via the Patent Pro Bono Coverage Map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the coverage map, select your state to apply directly to the regional program serving your state. Links go to regional (third-party) program websites where the actual application is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer practitioner eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent attorneys and agents are needed to volunteer to serve inventors and small business owners facing financial obstacles to obtaining patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteers should select their state in the Patent Pro Bono Coverage Map to submit an online volunteer application form. Participation requirements and volunteer onboarding processes are managed by the regional programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLE credit eligibility for volunteers
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent attorneys who volunteer for the Patent Pro Bono Program may be eligible for CLE credit through state bar associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys admitted to the bar in any state should check with their state bar association to determine whether their participation qualifies for CLE credit; eligibility and reporting procedures depend on the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Pro Bono Program matching criteria (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB Pro Bono Program matches qualifying underresourced patent applicants with volunteer patent professionals to provide free legal assistance for ex parte appeals (of final rejections by patent examiners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTAB Pro Bono Program is administered by the PTAB Bar Association; qualifying criteria and application procedures are handled by that program (seek its guidance for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Pro Bono Clearinghouse recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The TTAB Pro Bono Clearinghouse Program recognizes organizations that coordinate free legal assistance to those with proceedings before the TTAB and who might not otherwise have affordable access to legal assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each recognized clearinghouse organization has different requirements for accepting new clients and matches eligible clients with volunteer attorneys—contact the specific clearinghouse for its client-eligibility rules and application process.
